summary: Union-find (disjoint-set union) maintains a partition of elements into groups and supports two operations: find which group an element belongs to, and union two groups. With two simple optimizations, each operation takes nearly constant amortized time.

sections.heading: Representation
sections.body: Each set is a tree stored in a parent array. A root points to itself and acts as the set's representative. Two elements are in the same set iff they have the same root.
sections.code:
int parent[N], rnk[N];
void make_sets(int n) { for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { parent[i] = i; rnk[i] = 0; } }

sections.heading: Find with path compression
sections.body: Walk up to the root, then point every visited node directly at it, flattening the tree for future queries.

sections.heading: Union by rank
sections.body: Attach the shallower tree under the deeper one so trees stay short. Without it, a bad sequence of unions can create a chain with O(n) finds.

sections.heading: Complexity
bullets: With union by rank and path compression: amortized O(α(n)) per operation, where α is the inverse Ackermann function (below 5 for any practical n).

sections.heading: What it is used for
bullets: Cycle detection in undirected graphs (an edge joining two nodes with the same root closes a cycle).
Connected components, including dynamic ones as edges arrive.
Percolation and image segmentation, equivalence classes, grouping accounts.

sections.body: Start with {a}, {b}, {c}, {d}. unite(a,b), unite(b,d) gives {a,b,d}, {c}. find(a) == find(d), so a and d are connected; find(a) != find(c).
Attach the smaller set to the larger and track set sizes. It gives the same bounds and lets you query the size of a component for free.
Start with n components; each successful union (roots differ) reduces the count by one. At the end the counter holds the number of connected components.
On huge inputs the recursive find may overflow the stack. Do two loops: find the root, then walk again compressing the path.
Standard union-find supports merging but not splitting a set. For deletions or undo you need a rollback variant (no path compression) or offline techniques.

takeaways: Parent-array forests: find returns the root, union links roots.
Path compression + union by rank/size give near-O(1) amortized operations.
Core tool for Kruskal's MST and connected components.
It supports merges only, not splits.
